records.title: Wan 3.0
records.summary: Alibaba's hosted video generation family on Model Studio. Wan 3.0 comes in two ids, wan3.0-video and wan3.0-video-prime, at 480P, 720P and 1080P.
records.why_it_matters: It led the Artificial Analysis text-to-video board on 2026-11-12, and its 1080P list price is lower than Seedance 2.5 or FLUX 3 Video at 1080p.
records.fit_notes: Input video is billed too: billable seconds are input plus output, so a video-to-video edit with a 10 s input and a 10 s output bills 20 s. The 30 s free quota exists only in the Singapore region and only for wan3.0-video, and is valid for 90 days from activation, model release or approval, whichever is later. The 30% discount is labelled limited-time with no end date on the page. Maximum duration and whether audio is generated are not on the pricing page; OpenRouter lists 2-30 s for its resold copy, not checked at Alibaba.

related.note: resold as alibaba/wan-3.0 at the same list price

claims.text: In the Singapore region wan3.0-video lists at $0.05 per second at 480P, $0.1 at 720P and $0.2 at 1080P, shown with a limited-time 30% discount, and carries a 30 second free quota valid for 90 days from Model Studio activation, model release or application approval, whichever is later.

records.title: HappyHorse
records.summary: A second Alibaba video family on Model Studio, with text-to-video, first-frame image-to-video and reference-to-video ids per version.
records.why_it_matters: It is the cheapest way found here to try an Alibaba video model at 480P, with a small free quota.
records.fit_notes: On the Artificial Analysis boards read 2026-11-12, HappyHorse ranks well below Wan 3.0 (text-to-video rank 20 for 1.0). Pick Wan 3.0 for quality; HappyHorse 1.1 at 480P is a cheap draft step. Free quota is Singapore-only. Clip length and audio not on the pricing page.

records.title: Dreamina Seedance 2.5
records.summary: ByteDance's video generation family on BytePlus ModelArk. Seedance 2.5 (id dreamina-seedance-2-5-260628) generates up to 30 seconds with audio from text, frames or up to 50 reference assets, and edits or extends video.
records.why_it_matters: It ranked first on the Artificial Analysis image-to-video board read 2026-11-12 and gives the longest single clip found here (30 s).
records.fit_notes: Priced in tokens, not seconds: tokens = (input + output seconds) x width x height x fps / 1024. BytePlus' own worked example is $0.231/s at 720p 16:9 and $0.569/s at 1080p. Activation needs a BytePlus balance above USD 30, a savings plan or a resource pack, so there is no free try. BytePlus serves the docs as markdown (append .md) and lists an agent-skills index and an MCP server card at ai.byteplus.com/.well-known; those were not opened. OpenRouter resells it at 480p and 720p only.

claims.text: Seedance 2.5 generates up to 30 seconds in one request, can extend a video over several rounds and accepts up to 50 reference assets.
claims.quote: It can generate up to 30 seconds of video in one request, extend videos over multiple rounds, accept up to 50 omni reference assets per request, and perform precise timestamp-based editing.
claims.locator: Seedance 2.5 tutorial, intro paragraph

claims.text: The 1080p 5 second example costs $2.843, which BytePlus gives as $0.569 per second; 720p is $0.231 per second and 480p $0.103.
claims.quote: | Dreamina Seedance 2.5 | * $0.514 per video | * $1.156 per video | * $2.843 per video | \ | | * $0.103 per second | * $0.231 per second | * $0.569 per second |
claims.locator: Model pricing, Billing examples, Dreamina Seedance 2.5 series, tab Input without video (480p, 720p, 1080p, 16:9, 5 s)

claims.text: Before Seedance 2.5 can be enabled the account needs a balance above USD 30, a USD 30 savings plan or a resource pack.
claims.quote: **Recommended:** BytePlus account balance > USD 30
claims.locator: Seedance 2.5 tutorial, note before enabling the model

checked.what: BytePlus Seedance 2.5 tutorial and ModelArk pricing page, markdown versions, against all three claims

records.title: Seedream 5.0

records.title: Runway Gen-4.5
records.summary: Runway's own video generation model on the Runway Dev API, billed in credits per second.
records.why_it_matters: It is one of two models Runway lets export ProRes, PNG sequences and HDR, which matters when the output goes into a grading or compositing tool.
records.fit_notes: 12 credits = $0.12 per second. ProRes or PNG sequence adds 5 credits/s; HDR adds 20 credits/s (40 above 4 MP). OpenRouter resells it at the same 12 cents per second and lists 2-10 s at 720p. No free tier stated on the pricing page.

claims.text: Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits per second, and credits cost $0.01, so $0.12 per second.
claims.quote: gen4.5 | 12 credits per second
claims.locator: API pricing page, Video Generation Pricing table

claims.text: Professional and HDR output formats are available on Gen-4.5 and Aleph 2.0 and add a per-second surcharge.

claims.locator: API pricing page, section Professional and HDR output formats

records.title: Luma Ray3.2
records.summary: Luma's video generation model on the Luma API, with keyframes, video-to-video, reframe and HDR or EXR output.
records.why_it_matters: Native HDR and 16-bit EXR export are rare among hosted models and matter when the clip is composited with live footage.
records.fit_notes: The pricing page gives credits only, with no dollar value per credit, so the dollar cost cannot be worked out from it. 1080p text- or image-to-video for 10 s is 1,200 credits SDR (1,440 for video-to-video); HDR doubles it. The docs page opened (docs.lumalabs.ai video-generation) shows ray-2 examples, not Ray3.2 ids, so the exact Ray3.2 model id was not confirmed. Audio not stated.

claims.locator: API pricing page, Cost Breakdown, Ray3.2 tab

records.title: FLUX 3
records.summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 family on the BFL API: FLUX 3 Video for text, image or video input, and FLUX 3 Image for text or image input.
records.why_it_matters: Its pricing page states video rates for four resolution bands, whether audio is included, and the longest output.
records.fit_notes: Video-to-video costs more than text- or image-to-video at every band ($0.27 vs $0.24 at FHD). Draft mode at $0.06/s exists only in HD; a Draft Enhance render is billed as a full generation. FLUX 3 Image at 4K jumps to $0.607 per image, six times the 2K price. Exact API model ids were not read; docs.bfl.ai was not opened.

records.title: Nano Banana (Gemini image models)
records.summary: Google's image generation models on the Gemini API: gemini-nano-banana-2.1 and gemini-3-pro-image. Imagen 4 was shut down on the Gemini API and points to Nano Banana 2.1.
records.why_it_matters: Code that calls the GA imagen-4.0-*-001 ids on the Gemini API stopped working on 2026-08-17 (the preview ids on 2026-02-17); Nano Banana 2.1 is the named replacement.
records.fit_notes: Billed in output tokens; Google converts to per-image prices. Nano Banana 2.1 is $0.0336 per 1K image, gemini-3-pro-image $0.134 per 1K or 2K image, four times more. Neither has a free tier on the Gemini API. Batch halves the Nano Banana 2.1 price. fal resells Nano Banana Pro at $0.15 per image, above Google's own $0.134.

records.title: HeyGen Video 1
records.summary: HeyGen's general-purpose video generation model, built on MiniMax H3 and post-trained by HeyGen. It makes the scene and its sound in one call.
records.why_it_matters: It led the silent text-to-video board on Artificial Analysis read 2026-11-12, and it returns dialogue, ambience and effects with the clip.
records.fit_notes: Only the generation model is in scope here, not HeyGen avatars. The page gives no dollar price; OpenRouter lists $0.036 per second at 768p and $0.10 at 1080p, which is close to the stated 3x. Runs on paid API keys only. Unknown request fields are rejected, so copy field names exactly.

related.note: HeyGen says it is built on MiniMax H3

claims.quote: Text-to-video and image-to-video clips can run 5 to 30 seconds with compatible settings; reference-to-video stays at 5 to 15 seconds. Each clip has its own audio track of dialogue, ambience and sound effects
